title: Fano leaves and planar glue
claim: For a connected 3-regular triple system H with distinct points per line that is not 2-colourable (the dual of a three-fold space of the knot): (1) The approved grammar is incomplete. Three twisted 14-point pieces placed on the cube (a Kasteleyn sign pattern, one negation per face) give a 43-point system whose tight-cut decomposition contains the cube as a brace, while every system built from Fano planes by splices and (twisted) cycles of Fano blocks decomposes into Heawood graphs and doubled squares only; brace lists are unique (Lovasz). (2) Structure: tight cuts of the incidence graph are 3-edge cuts with cubic contractions; a brace with a repeated incidence is the 4-vertex doubled square (sign-nonsingular exactly with an odd number of negated classes); every leaf is a simple cubic brace signed trivially except possibly one negated edge at its contracted vertex; every brace carries an induced Pfaffian signing. (3) Every Pfaffian brace other than the Heawood graph has, for each 4-cycle, an edge-disjoint 4-cycle (planar braces by Euler's formula, the rest by induction over the Robertson-Seymour-Thomas trisum structure), so a brace on at least six vertices with a Pfaffian signing negating at most one edge is the Heawood graph signed trivially. (4) Fano leaves: every leaf of every tight-cut decomposition is a Fano plane minus a line (attached at its points) or minus a point (attached at its lines); H, unless it is the Fano plane, contains at least two vertex-disjoint such pieces. (5) Decoration: every cubic multi-system with a sign-nonsingular signing becomes a non-colourable triple system with distinct points per line when its signed and repeated points are replaced by twisted 14-point pieces and Fano blocks; so every planar cubic bipartite graph (Kasteleyn) is the core of three-fold knot spaces (cube 43, hexagonal prism 45, truncated octahedron 90, the 3-cycle core 21, the tripod core 22 points).
failure_conditions: A system built by splices and cycles of Fano blocks with a brace other than Heawood graphs and doubled squares.
A brace with a repeated incidence on more than four vertices, or a leaf that is not simple.

A Pfaffian brace other than the Heawood graph with a 4-cycle that shares an edge with every other 4-cycle, or a brace on at least six vertices other than the trivially signed Heawood graph with a sign-nonsingular signing negating at most one edge.
A leaf of a tight-cut decomposition that is not a Heawood graph.
A signed core that decorates to a 2-colourable system, or a computation that does not reproduce.
foundation_claim_scope: Cubic triple systems with distinct or repeated points per line, their incidence graphs, tight cuts, Pfaffian signings and decorations; the knot reading via the duality of SPACE-SELECTION-20261030-001C. The Robertson-Seymour-Thomas structure theorem (6.8 and its proof) and Kasteleyn's signings are external inputs, not replayed.

validation.status: checked: twisted cube and generated systems decomposed (brace lists); structure on all computed decompositions; doubled-square signings; one-twist lemma and the 4-cycle partner property on the Heawood graph, three planar braces and two non-planar cubic trisums (16 and 24 vertices, one Pfaffian class each); Fano pieces on every constructed system; five decorations non-colourable by SAT, the smaller ones minimal; controls fire; no human or external review
validation.novelty: classical inputs: Lovasz's tight-cut decomposition and uniqueness of braces, Pfaffian contractions, Robertson-Seymour-Thomas 1999 (Theorem 6.8, trisums), Kasteleyn's planar signings; the 4-cycle partner property is stated by Gorsky, Johanni and Wiederrecht (arXiv 2408.08128, Lemma 3.4; their proof not read); no overlap found (candidate local delta) for the one-twist lemma, the Fano-leaf theorem and the decoration theorem in this setting, and the reading as the knot's three-fold spaces
